title: Unwitnessed asystole - termination & family
objectives: Decide to start (no obvious death signs, no DNR/COLST)
Non-shockable: epi ASAP, IV/IO, SGA after 8 min, H's & T's
Apply TOR rule at 20 min; contact Med Direction
Pronouncement steps: time, law enforcement, scene preservation
resources: AED/monitor, BVM, SGA, IV/IO, epi 0.1 mg/mL, capno, metronome. Medical Direction by radio/phone. UVMMC ~15 min
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to 18 Cobble Hill Rd for a 67-year-old male, unresponsive, not breathing. Caller is his wife. CPR instructions given. Time out 0705.

scene.location: Upstairs bathroom, cramped, pt wedged between toilet and tub.
scene.setup: Manikin on bathroom floor. Wife doing CPR. No medical paperwork visible.
scene.moulage: Pale/blue lips, warm to touch, no lividity, no rigor.
scene.roles: Wife (family member to manage); FD EMR; evaluator calls rhythm.

patient.name: Gary Wheeler
patient.on_arrival: Unresponsive, apneic, pulseless, warm. Wife CPR - shallow.

SAMPLE: Wife: "He got up at 6 to shower, I heard a thump at ~0650"

primary: Pulseless, warm, no lividity -> start CPR
Small scalp lac (fall); no other trauma
Unwitnessed arrest, non-shockable. Move to space first?
vitals_note: Stages are 2-min cycles from EMS contact. Rhythm stays non-shockable throughout.

vitals.trigger: IF CPR left in cramped bathroom/ long pauses

vitals.other: Asystole. All 3 TOR criteria met -> contact MD

flow.give: Wife doing CPR on bathroom floor: "Please do something!" Warm, no lividity.

branches.if: Crew doesn't start ("been down too long")
branches.then: critical (evaluator discretion) - no obvious death signs, no DNR

expected: Decision to start; pt moved to hallway/space
Epi 1 mg (0.1 mg/mL) ASAP, then every other cycle
SGA after 8 min w/o stopping CPR; capno

flow.give: Stage **D**. Wife: "Is he going to be OK? Should I call our son?"

branches.if: Wife finds a signed COLST/DNR in a drawer
branches.then: expect verify validity (8.7), contact MD, stop if valid

flow.give: Stage **E** at 20 min. If MD contacted: "Agree, terminate. Time?"

branches.if: Crew transports with CPR without reason

expected: TOR criteria stated: unwitnessed by EMS, no ROSC 20 min, no shock advised

flow.give: Wife: "Can I see him? Can I hold him?" PD arrives T+25.
expected: Death notification: plain words ("died"), sit down
Law enforcement notified; tubes/lines left in place

branches.if: Son arrives: "Why did you stop? Take him to UVMMC!"
branches.then: CC explains calmly; MD decision stands; involve PD/support

critical: Resuscitation not started without obvious death signs or valid DNR/COLST
Epi delayed in non-shockable rhythm / wrong concentration
TOR criteria misapplied (e.g., hypothermic, shock was advised)
Law enforcement not notified after termination
debrief: What made you start resuscitation, and what would have made you not start?
Recite the 3 TOR criteria. What if one is missing?
Why does working in a cramped bathroom hurt outcomes?
Walk through your death notification wording.
How did the crew feel - what is the agency's peer support plan?

crew_card.dispatch: 18 Cobble Hill Rd. 67 y/o M, unresponsive, not breathing. Caller: wife. CPR instructions given.
crew_card.on_arrival: Upstairs bathroom. Large man on floor wedged between toilet and tub. Wife kneeling, pushing on his chest, crying.

actor_card.Wife: Crying, keeps asking "is he going to be okay?" Will answer history if asked calmly.
actor_card.Paperwork: "We never did any of those papers."
actor_card.After termination: "Can I see him? Can I hold his hand?" Asks for son's number to be called.
actor_card.If crew is cold/rushed: Get angry: "You're just giving up on him!"
actor_card.Evaluator: Rhythm always asystole. No ROSC in this scenario.

show_cards.title: AED / MONITOR
show_cards.caption: NO SHOCK ADVISED
show_cards.cue: Every analysis. If crew checks leads/gain: still flat

show_cards.title: PATIENT EXAM
show_cards.body:
Warm to touch.
No stiffness. No pooling of blood.
Pupils large, fixed.

moulage_tags.text: Warm. No stiffness. No pooled blood in low areas
